---
title: "🔍 Data quality, diversity and fleets"
description: >
  data_quality(), diversity_concentration(), country_group_summary() and coastal_distant():
  how reliable the data are, how diverse and concentrated the catch is, and who is fishing.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("_setup.R")
FAO34 <- suppressMessages(fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Eastern Central", plot = FALSE))
```

```{r data-source, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
data_source()
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
FAO34 <- fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Eastern Central")
```

## 🧪 Data quality

`data_quality()` shows two aspects of the statistics over time:

- the share of the catch **reported officially**, and the share **estimated** (by the country or
  imputed by FAO), from the FAO status flags;
- the share of the catch **identified to species**, genus, family, or only to a higher group such as
  "Marine fishes nei", from the FAO taxonomic codes.

```{r, figures = TRUE}
quality <- data_quality(FAO34$area_data)
```

A large estimated share in the latest years usually means that FAO has not yet received the
national reports; these values are often revised in the next release. The country table shows,
for the countries with the largest catch in the last five years, how much was estimated and how
much identified to species:

```{r}
show_table(quality$countries, digits = 1)
```

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `top_n` | Number of countries in the country table | `10` |

## 🌈 Diversity and concentration

`diversity_concentration()` computes, for each year:

| Indicator | Calculation |
|---|---|
| Number of species reported | Items identified to species with catch |
| Number of countries | Countries with catch |
| Shannon diversity | $H = -\sum_i p_i \ln p_i$, with $p_i$ the share of species item $i$ in the year's catch |
| HHI of species / countries | $\text{HHI} = \sum_i (100\,p_i)^2$, from 0 to 10 000 |
| Top-N share | Share of the `top_n` largest species items or countries |

```{r, figures = TRUE}
diversity <- diversity_concentration(FAO34$area_data, top_n = 5)
```

```{r}
show_table(subset(diversity, Year %in% c(1970, 1990, 2010, max(Year))), digits = 2)
```

**Reading the indicators.** A higher Shannon index means more species items and a more even catch;
its maximum is $\ln S$ for $S$ items. An HHI below 1 500 is usually read as unconcentrated, 1 500
to 2 500 as moderately and above 2 500 as highly concentrated. For example, three species with
shares of 50%, 30% and 20% give $H = 1.03$ and $\text{HHI} = 50^2 + 30^2 + 20^2 = 3\,800$.

::: callout-note
The indicators use FAO species items, including "nei" groups. When FAO splits a "nei" group into
species, Shannon diversity rises and HHI falls even if nothing changed at sea. Country indicators
change when countries split, e.g. the USSR in 1991.
:::

## 🏳️ Country groups

`country_group_summary()` sums the catch by groups of countries from the FAO country list:
**World Bank income group**, **continent** or **region**.

```{r, figures = TRUE}
income <- country_group_summary(FAO34$area_data, group = "income")
```

```{r, figures = TRUE}
country_group_summary(FAO34$area_data, group = "region", top_n = 6, lang = "zh")
```

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `group` | `"income"`, `"continent"` or `"region"` | `"income"` |
| `top_n` | Number of groups shown separately | `8` |

## 🚢 Coastal countries and distant-water fleets

`coastal_distant()` splits the catch between countries that **border** the fishing area and
**distant-water** fleets from elsewhere, and shows the main distant-water countries.

A country is coastal to an area if its land (including overseas territories) lies within 20 km of
the FAO area boundary. Former countries such as the USSR take the coastline of their successor
states. In area 34, for example, Spain and Portugal count as coastal because of the Canary Islands
and Madeira.

```{r, figures = TRUE}
fleets <- coastal_distant(FAO34$area_data)
```

```{r}
show_table(fleets$table, digits = 0)
```

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `top_n` | Number of distant-water countries shown separately | `8` |

The analysis works for marine areas; inland areas in the data are left out with a message.
